lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: You're listening to Saturday Night Forever, one oh eight point four. It's Saturday night. It has been for a while. Nobody minds.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Saturday Night Forever, from the Starlite Rollerdrome, where the night is young. It's been young for a very long time.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: This is Donna Midnight, on Saturday Night Forever. Skates on, lights low, and nobody, but nobody, is asking what time it is.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Saturday Night Forever. The mirror ball is turning, the floor is lit, and Sunday is just a rumour.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Saturday Night Forever. If it's daytime where you are, that's fine, honey. We don't judge. In here, it's Saturday night.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: One oh eight point four, Saturday Night Forever. Way out at the edge of the dial, where the party never got the memo.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Some of you newer skaters have been asking about the clock over the rink. The one with no hands. We voted the hands off, back in hour forty.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: It was close. The minute hand gave a lovely speech. But the hour hand kept looking at people, and honey, nobody likes to be looked at like that on a Saturday.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: News of the conga line. It left the rink in hour nine hundred, out through the fire doors, and it hasn't come back.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: We got a postcard this week. It's three counties north now, and still going. Still a conga. Still on the beat. Wherever you are, conga line, we're proud of you.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Over by the snack bar, Brenda and Lou, who met in hour six, and have been on their first date ever since.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: It's going very well. He's about to ask her to skate. He's been about to ask for a long time. Don't rush him. In here, there's no such thing as too late.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Some of the regulars say there's a thing that comes after Saturday. They call it Sunday. Church bells, a roast dinner, a sort of quiet headache.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: I don't believe a word of it, honey. Sounds made up. Here's a song that definitely isn't.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: The mirror ball has gone round about four hundred million times tonight. People worry. Isn't it dizzy?

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: We asked it. It said, honey, I'm a mirror ball. Going round is the job. Then it threw a little light on my shoes, which I thought was very sweet.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Let's check in with Rollo, our rink guard. Rollo, how's the floor?

lines.speaker: Rollo, the Rink Guard
lines.text: Busy, Donna. Everyone's going counter-clockwise. Nobody's going backwards. Lovely night.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: That's the thing about a night that never ends, honey. It only goes one way.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Bev. Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Bev, honey, it's Saturday night. Everything's the request line. What can I play for you?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I don't know what it's called. It goes, da da dum. Da da.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Oh, we play that one every night, Bev. You stay on the floor. It's coming.

clips.title: A Light Over the Car Park

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: There's a new light in the sky over the car park. A relay ship, drifted in from somewhere further up the dial. Hello, newcomer.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Skate hire's free after hour three million. Come on down. And leave your watch in the ship. You won't be needing it.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Somebody has to dust the mirror ball, and tonight that somebody is standing on a ladder from Grumbel's.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: And down, honey, is the next song.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Out there it's evening, and people are doing their hair. That's sweet. In here, we did our hair in nineteen seventy seven, and it has held.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Every curl. Every wave. If you're getting ready, take your time. We'll still be here. We're always still here.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: A newcomer asked me the time earlier. The whole rink went quiet. Even the mirror ball slowed down.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Then the drummer laughed, and we all laughed, and I bought her a lemonade. Honey, it's Saturday. That's the time.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Time check, everybody. Donna Midnight, with the hours.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: It's that time again. Not the time, honey. We don't do the time. The count.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hands up if you've lost track. Good. That's my job. Here's the count.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hour three million, four hundred and six thousand, and twelve. Still Saturday.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: The ice in my lemonade has started to think about melting. Only thinking. I'll keep you posted.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: We have now been dancing for three million, four hundred thousand hours. That's about three hundred and eighty years, give or take a slow song.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: And nobody in this room looks a day over Saturday.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hour three million, four hundred and seven thousand. To celebrate, the snack bar has turned the hot dog over.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: It's been the same hot dog since hour one. It's a very good hot dog. It's had a lot of time to think about it.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hour three million and, ooh. I'll be honest, I lost count for a second there, in the drum break. It happens.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Luckily Rollo keeps a backup, written on his wrist in biro. Rollo? Thank you, honey. We're right on track.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hour three million, four hundred and six thousand, five hundred and fifty. Somebody's grandmother just did the splits.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: She's been here since hour one. She was nineteen when she came in. And honey, in every way that matters, she still is.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Three million, four hundred and six thousand, eight hundred hours, and not a single one of them has been a Monday.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Think about that. Then don't. Thinking is for Sundays.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: That's the count. Don't write it down. It'll be wrong in an hour.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Still Saturday, everybody. Back on the floor.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: And that's the time, honey. It's tonight. It's always tonight.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: This is the Hustle Hour, on Saturday Night Forever! Find a space, find a partner, find your feet. In that order.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Hustle lesson, for the newcomers. Step one, step to the left. Step two, step back. Step three, point at the mirror ball like it owes you money.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Step four, do it all again, for three hundred years. You're a natural, honey.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: The line dance in the middle of the rink started in hour two hundred. It's forty thousand hours long. There are steps in it nobody has seen yet.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: If you join in now, you'll get to the good bit in about eleven years. Worth it. I've heard there's a spin.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Lights down, everybody. It's Couples Skate. Find someone you've been dancing next to for eleven years, and introduce yourself.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Oh, look at that. Lou has asked Brenda to skate. He asks her every Couples Skate, and every Couples Skate, she says yes, like it's the first time.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: They're going round now, slowly, holding hands. That's about forty thousand first dates, honey. And not one of them has been a bad one.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: To everyone sitting this one out on the carpet benches. That's all right too. Rest your feet. Hold your lemonade.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Somebody has to watch. A night this long needs witnesses.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Good morning, out there. This is Breakfast at the Rink. You've got the sunrise. We've got pancakes, and a mirror ball. It's a fair trade.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: We call this breakfast, but it's still Saturday night in here. The snack bar started doing pancakes in hour three thousand, because somebody asked.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: And on a Saturday night, honey, nobody ever says no.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: A word for everyone out there in the morning. Your night ended. That's all right. Nights do. Ours didn't.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: So we're keeping it for you. Come back tonight, and it'll be right where you left it. Same song, same floor. Same us.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Forever Hold Hairspray. Holds for one night. Any night. This night.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: I've used it since nineteen seventy seven, honey. I haven't touched my hair since. I'm not allowed to. It's load bearing.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Forever Hold. Keep away from mirror balls. They get ideas.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Starlite Skate Hire, at the counter by the snack bar. Wheels for every foot. Sizes four to fourteen.

lines.speaker: Rollo, the Rink Guard
lines.text: Size nine's out. Size nine's been out since hour eleven. He's very good. He's not giving them back.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Starlite Skate Hire. Return your skates when the night ends.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: A message from the management of the Starlite Rollerdrome.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Please don't ask the time. Not because we're hiding it. Because the last person who asked made the drummer cry, and he's very good, and we need him.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Thank you, management.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Did anybody catch the Quiet Corner, over on the Lounge at the End of Time? Greg's show. I had my ear right up against the speaker.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: I heard one word. I think it was, lovely. Five stars, Greg. Turn it up a little, honey. Come and dance.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Somebody's just skated in from the car park saying a moon has gone missing. Honey, we haven't looked at the sky since nineteen seventy seven.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: We'll take your word for it. This one's for the moon, wherever she's dancing tonight.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Can everybody smell toast? The whole rink smells of toast. The snack bar swears it isn't them. They don't do toast. They do one hot dog.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Keep skating, everybody. Breathe it in.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Everyone on the floor is humming the same song, and nobody can remember how it ends. Bev's here. Bev's crying. Bev says that's the one.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: If anybody knows the last line, come up to the booth.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Three knocks on the booth door, just now. Rollo went to look. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: Rollo, the Rink Guard
lines.text: Might be Sunday, Donna.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Then don't open it, Rollo. Not tonight.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: The skylight's gone a colour I don't have a word for. And I have a lot of words for colours, honey. I've got eleven for gold.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: The mirror ball's throwing it all over the floor. Everybody looks wonderful in it.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: There's a pigeon on the rink. It's going round counter-clockwise, like everybody. It just nodded at me like it knew me.

lines.speaker: Donna Midnight
lines.text: Maybe it does. It's been a long night.
